newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S FORMER PRIME MINISTER SHOT DEAD.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S FORMER PRIME MINISTER SHOT DEAD.

text.p: Bulgaria's former Prime Minister Andrei Lukanov, who is now a deputy of the ruling Socialists, was found shot dead at his home, parlament's speaker said on Wednesday.
Blagovest Sendov told parliament on opening its session on Wednesday morning that circumstances of Lukanov's death were still not clear.
Sendov appealed to the deputies to keep calm and closed the parliamentary session.
The interior ministry and police declined any further information.
The whole area where Lukanov lives in Sofia is surrounded by police. Neighbours, who declined to be named, told Reuters he was shot with two bullets in the head while going out from his house.
Lukanov, 58, now an influential businessman, served as an ex-communist prime minister for six months in 1990. He resigned due to widespread public dissatisfaction with the sluggish pace of reform.

In July Lukanov was dropped as board chairman of a Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company, Topenergy, in a move designed to improve its troubled relations with the Bulgarian government. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
